findings.Quote: She turned it over once more, because it was worth turning over, and that was where she felt why she wouldn't take it.

findings.Fix: Trim to 'The literature was thin, mostly the shape of where research used to be.'

findings.Quote: and she knew exactly how the word got there and how little it told you about why
findings.Fix: Trim the second clause or make it more specific to Yemina's situation rather than a general aphorism about record-keeping.

findings.Quote: the way the highlights in Kito's care record had been waiting
findings.Fix: Either establish this comparison earlier with enough weight to bear the callback, or cut it—as is it reads as a reminder note rather than an earned echo.

findings.Quote: the readiness of a person who'd been listening for it longer than made sense
findings.Note: tells the reader an emotional/character judgment rather than showing it, and 'longer than made sense' is vague filler explaining nothing concrete
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete observed detail, e.g. 'she'd left the chain off the door.'

findings.Quote: the woman standing among them had the look of someone who'd spent two years alone with a shape nobody else believed in
findings.Note: abstract 'look of someone who' construction tells the backstory instead of showing a physical detail
findings.Fix: ground it in a specific visual: unwashed hair, a cot in the corner, etc.

findings.Quote: That was rarer than competence.
findings.Note: universal-truth quip asserted without support, functions as authorial commentary rather than observation
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete comparison to someone else Yemina has interviewed

findings.Quote: the stack settling with the slump of paper that had been lifted and replaced ten thousand times
findings.Note: the hyperbolic 'ten thousand times' undercuts the otherwise concrete image with an unverifiable, decorative exaggeration
findings.Fix: cut to 'the stack settling with the slump of paper lifted and replaced too many times'

findings.Quote: Three districts with no reason to agree, agreeing.
findings.Note: Sentence-fragment aphorism used for portentous effect; slightly overplays the beat's own logic after already stating it plainly.
findings.Fix: Cut, or fold into the prior sentence: 'The markers held their relationship to the schools anyway, three districts with no reason to agree.'

findings.Quote: It was true, and it was nothing, and they both heard which of the two it was.
findings.Note: Aphoristic construction that tells us the emotional weight rather than showing it; slightly too neat/pseudo-profound for the moment.
findings.Fix: Cut the final clause or replace with a concrete beat (a look, a silence) rather than the summarizing triplet.

findings.Quote: where only someone who already knew the case was urgent could reach it
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought explanatory aside that tells the reader the irony instead of trusting the menu-maze to demonstrate it.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause and let the four-level descent speak for itself.

findings.Quote: It wasn't for her. It was for the file — so that later, if anyone asked, the record would show the caller had been informed.
findings.Note: Explains the system's cynicism in flat exposition rather than letting the detail (excluded criteria) carry it; slightly over-tells what's already implied.
findings.Fix: Cut the last sentence or compress to one clause.

findings.Quote: because inflection gave a listener somewhere to be skeptical, and a flat voice reading verified numbers was the one kind of statement this system couldn't file under *distressed caller.*
findings.Note: Borders on aphoristic explanation of her tactic rather than showing it; reads as authorial gloss on cleverness.
findings.Fix: Trim to the concrete action and let the italicized phrase alone carry the irony.

findings.Quote: The same shape as every gap she'd ever found: a quantity the system tracked, beside a quantity it didn't, with exactly enough room between them to lose someone in.
findings.Note: Reads as a summarizing aphorism restating the chapter's thesis rather than advancing thought; slightly pseudo-profound in cadence.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in a concrete prior instance she's recalling.

findings.Quote: each stroke gone over twice the way a child goes over a letter to make it certain
findings.Note: Explains the child's motive/psychology via simile rather than showing it; slightly tautological (defines 'certain' by the action meant to illustrate it).
findings.Fix: Cut the 'way a child goes over a letter' clause and let the doubled strokes stand alone.

findings.Quote: a location given as a promise instead of a coordinate
findings.Note: abstract phrasing that restates the point rather than sharpening it; slightly overworked
findings.Fix: cut to one clause: 'Not a coordinate. A promise.'

findings.Quote: Silence was not an answer. She'd learned that fifteen years ago and relearned it every year since, and it still cost her something each time.
findings.Note: drifts into aphorism/telling-not-showing territory, stating an emotional lesson rather than dramatizing it
findings.Fix: trim to concrete cost: cut the generalized 'learned/relearned' clause and show what it cost her this time

findings.Quote: a known quantity, a thing with a beginning and an end that arrived on schedule no matter what she understood or didn't
findings.Note: slightly over-explains the metaphor already made clear by the four-minutes repetition, risking redundancy
findings.Fix: trim to 'a known quantity, a thing that arrived on schedule no matter what she understood or didn't'

findings.Quote: A report was not the place for the things that had no field. A report was the place for what you could stand behind if someone read it back to you in a hearing room five years from now.
findings.Note: borders on aphoristic double-statement restating the same idea twice for emphasis, slightly tips into telling-the-theme
findings.Fix: cut the first sentence and keep only the hearing-room line, or vice versa

findings.Quote: because cones were the only object the city kept in inventory for a hazard it had no real object for
findings.Note: clever-sounding but circular phrasing that restates itself instead of landing a point
findings.Fix: because cones were the only tool the city had for a problem it had no tool for

findings.Quote: It was a number that had already been prepared, sitting somewhere, waiting for her to finish typing so it could be handed to her.
findings.Note: Slightly over-explains the inference the reader already grasped from the preceding sentence; borders on telling.
findings.Fix: Cut to: 'It was a number already prepared, waiting for her to finish typing.'

findings.Quote: in the flat administrative voice of a system that had never once apologized for anything
findings.Note: Personifying the system with a quip about apology reads as a stray aphorism rather than concrete description.
findings.Fix: Cut the apology clause or replace with a literal detail of the notice's formatting.

findings.Quote: because deciding early was how you missed the thing that mattered
findings.Note: Reads as a generalized maxim about investigation rather than specific to her situation — mild aphorism filler.
findings.Fix: Tie it to a concrete past instance rather than stating it as universal rule.

findings.Quote: had probably done that every day since the first visit
findings.Note: Tells us the inference rather than showing evidence for it; slightly padded explanatory aside.
findings.Fix: Cut 'probably' or ground it in a physical detail (worn path on the mat, etc.).

findings.Quote: "She'd thought, driving over, about what she'd say if asked what the notice said, and hadn't arrived at anything better than the truth, which was that it said almost nothing.
findings.Note: Stray open quotation mark starts the paragraph as if it were dialogue, but it's interior narration — a mechanical error, not just punctuation polish, since it misattributes the sentence as spoken.
findings.Fix: Remove the leading quotation mark: 'She'd thought, driving over...'

findings.Quote: The way you look at an envelope before you decide whether you have the strength to open it this week or next.
findings.Note: Generalizing aphoristic aside shifts from close third into a universal 'you' truism, softening the specific moment.
findings.Fix: Anchor it to Chinwe specifically: 'The way she looked at bills before deciding whether to open them this week or next.'

findings.Quote: An open case wasn't a door. It was a status.
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought abstraction-metaphor construction, though it mostly earns its keep by paying off concretely afterward.
findings.Fix: Could tighten to state the distinction more plainly without the door/status framing.

findings.Quote: It wasn't unkind. It was a fact being filed, in the order she'd learned it.
findings.Note: The second clause is vague filler that gestures at meaning without delivering concrete sense — unclear what 'the order she'd learned it' refers to.
findings.Fix: Cut the second clause or replace with a concrete detail about how she learned it.

findings.Quote: Chinwe asked it the way you ask a question you've already decided you can't survive a full answer to
findings.Note: Shifts into generalized second-person aphorism, telling the reader how to feel rather than showing Chinwe's specific manner
findings.Fix: Ground it in Chinwe's specific body/voice instead of a universalized 'you'

findings.Quote: she didn't know, and that not knowing was the most honest thing she had left to give
findings.Note: Verges on aphoristic self-summary that tells the reader the emotional takeaway rather than trusting the scene
findings.Fix: Cut the 'most honest thing she had left to give' clause and let the plain admission stand

findings.Quote: the way you nod at a scale reading you already suspected
findings.Note: simile aims for precision but reads as slightly overworked/pat given the plain register around it
findings.Fix: cut the simile or shorten to something less tidy, e.g. 'the way you nod at bad news you already knew.'

findings.Quote: a hinge oiled by someone who took care of what was theirs
findings.Note: purple/strained inference from a sound to character judgment about ownership and care; slightly overreaches literal plausibility
findings.Fix: trim to 'a hinge someone kept oiled' and cut the ownership claim

findings.Quote: the only object in the car that had anywhere left to go
findings.Note: reaches for poetic significance on the folder but is abstract to the point of muddiness — unclear literal meaning
findings.Fix: ground the image more concretely, e.g. describe the barcode catching light without the abstract 'anywhere left to go' claim

findings.Quote: A folder marked *no substitutions* outranked a parking ticket.
findings.Note: Cute aphoristic phrasing that tells rather than shows her priority calculus; slight quip-for-quip's-sake feel.
findings.Fix: Cut to plain action: "She left it. The folder mattered more."

findings.Quote: bright and patient
findings.Note: Personifying the panels as "patient" is a soft purple flourish that doesn't hold up to literal scrutiny — paint doesn't wait.
findings.Fix: Cut "and patient" or replace with a concrete detail, e.g. "bright, unweathered."

findings.Quote: Nobody looked at her the way people look at someone who doesn't belong. Nobody looked at her at all.
findings.Note: Circular/redundant construction states the same idea twice without adding information, reading as a rhetorical flourish rather than earned observation.
findings.Fix: Cut the first sentence and keep only the second, then build the explanation from there.

findings.Quote: Not the way you hold a heavy bag. The way you hold something you're keeping out of the wind.
findings.Note: The second-person 'you' address is a stylistic tic that tells the reader how to feel about the image rather than rendering it concretely through Yemina's perception.
findings.Fix: Rephrase in Yemina's close third: 'Not braced like weight. Cradled, like she was shielding it from wind.'

findings.Quote: She said it the way you hand over the one credential you've been told you can hand over.
findings.Note: Another second-person simile that explains the emotional/behavioral subtext rather than letting the flat delivery speak for itself; slightly redundant with the following 'Flat, complete, nothing behind it.'
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and keep 'Flat. Complete. Nothing behind it.'

findings.Quote: the folder joined to the thing she was already keeping from the wind that wasn't there
findings.Note: Callback to the wind image is serviceable but the phrasing is convoluted enough to slow the beat's tension at its most physical moment.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'the folder pressed against the bag she still hadn't let go of.'

findings.Quote: She wasn't keeping anything from Yemina. She had nothing to keep it with.
findings.Note: Cute aphoristic turn that tells us Nadia's inner state via wordplay rather than showing it; reads as authorial cleverness inserted into Yemina's POV.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence or ground it in a concrete observation Yemina makes.

findings.Quote: because it was the correct thing to say and she had nothing more correct to offer
findings.Note: Overexplains the line's motivation instead of trusting the dialogue tag; slightly precious phrasing.
findings.Fix: Trim to "because it was the correct thing to say."

findings.Quote: a real laugh
findings.Note: Vague qualifier that tells rather than shows what distinguishes this laugh from a fake one.
findings.Fix: Cut 'a real' or replace with a concrete physical detail.

findings.Quote: pleased with himself in the easy way of someone who liked making people laugh and didn't need more than the laugh for it
findings.Note: Abstract, explanatory characterization stated rather than dramatized; reads as authorial summary rather than observation.
findings.Fix: Trim to a physical beat, e.g., 'grinned, already looking for the next pallet.'

findings.Quote: or if they did, Yemina didn't hear it in the minute she watched him
findings.Note: Hedging qualifier undercuts the punchy simplicity of the preceding declaration and reads as filler clarification.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or shorten to 'if they did, she didn't hear it.'

findings.Quote: the way you watch a temperature drop on a gauge instead of feeling it on your skin
findings.Note: Simile is doing distancing/observation work but is abstract enough to slow the beat without adding sharper image than it costs in clarity.
findings.Fix: Cut to something more concrete: 'the way you watch weather move in on someone else's town.'

findings.Quote: the way a door closes when someone on the far side decides it should
findings.Note: Stock figurative construction for sudden emotional shift; reads as generic 'door closing' imagery despite the added clause.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific physical beat unique to the character, e.g., describe his jaw or hands stopping mid-motion.

findings.Quote: He had braced for exactly this and been caught off-guard all the same
findings.Note: Borders on paradox-as-profundity; states an internal contradiction as insight rather than dramatizing it.
findings.Fix: Show the physical contradiction (hand already reaching, feet stepping back) instead of stating the paradox.

findings.Quote: The least remarkable thing a freight dock produced in an hour.
findings.Note: Reads as an authorial summarizing quip that leans toward a tidy universal-truth cadence rather than continuing the scene's sensory grounding.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or fold its point into the preceding sentence without the aphoristic button.

findings.Quote: lighter by one folder now, and carried exactly the same
findings.Note: the observation strains to sound meaningful about a physical non-difference (a bag holding one less folder wouldn't visibly change how it's carried), reads as manufactured significance
findings.Fix: cut the clause or make the physical detail concrete (e.g., 'the bag rode a little looser against her chest')

findings.Quote: ran, at its far end, straight out of every registry she could see
findings.Note: vague spatial metaphor ('far end... straight out') that doesn't clarify what she actually now understands about the chain of custody
findings.Fix: specify what 'out of every registry' means in concrete terms, e.g., 'ended somewhere no registry logged'

findings.Quote: the way you hold a thing handed to you at a funeral
findings.Note: Simile gestures at solemnity without specifying any concrete funeral object or gesture; it explains the emotion rather than showing a precise physical image.
findings.Fix: Cut the comparison and describe the actual grip/posture instead.

findings.Quote: Her hand went to her wrist before she noticed she'd moved it.
findings.Note: Slightly redundant with the following sentence restating the same idea ("her hand found her wrist now on its own"), doubling up the same beat of unconscious action.
findings.Fix: Cut one of the two restatements of the involuntary gesture.

findings.Quote: His grip didn't tighten and didn't loosen.
findings.Note: Double-negative construction states the non-event twice without adding information, weakening the otherwise strong stillness beat.
findings.Fix: His grip stayed loose, unchanged.

findings.Quote: He wasn't fighting the urge to look. There was no urge.
findings.Note: Redundant restatement of the same idea back-to-back reads as padding rather than emphasis.
findings.Fix: Cut one of the two sentences.

findings.Quote: She had a word for what she'd have felt, standing where he stood, holding what he held. Watching him, she couldn't make the word fit.
findings.Note: Withholding the word for mystique reads as a coy authorial trick rather than earned tension; borders on purple abstraction.
findings.Fix: Either name the word or ground the failure to apply it in a concrete observation.

findings.Quote: She had no form it belonged on.
findings.Note: Metaphor (literal bureaucratic form vs. emotional exception) is serviceable but slightly overreaches into aphorism territory, especially stacked right after the quota/measurement setup.
findings.Fix: Trim to a more literal beat: 'There was nowhere to log it.'

findings.Quote: nothing that said he knew a woman by a gray car had been counting his stillness in seconds
findings.Note: overwrought phrasing for a simple observation; 'counting his stillness in seconds' is a purple flourish that draws attention to itself without earning it
findings.Fix: nothing that said he knew she'd been watching him at all

findings.Quote: the practiced care of a man who expects it to be there when he comes back, or expects someone else to come for it
findings.Note: telling-not-showing the significance of the gesture; the double hedge ('expects it to be there... or expects someone else') reads as authorial hand-wringing rather than observed detail
findings.Fix: tighten to a single concrete inference or cut the clause

findings.Quote: The shape of the thing — receive, hold, place, close — was familiar to his body.
findings.Note: abstract labeling of the action undercuts the scene's observational tension; states an interpretation rather than letting the action itself carry it
findings.Fix: cut or fold into a shorter observation, e.g. 'His body knew the motion already.'

findings.Quote: She could enter that. She could not enter it as anything other than what it was — a courier, a transfer, and a locked door in a freight yard
findings.Note: The 'enter that/enter it' wordplay is muddled — first 'enter' means log/record, second seems to mean physically open, but the referent shifts unclearly and reads as a stretch for parallelism rather than clarity.
findings.Fix: She could log that. She could not treat it as anything other than what it was — a courier, a transfer, a locked door in a freight yard.

findings.Quote: The case hadn't ended up somewhere. It had been put somewhere, by someone who expected it back.
findings.Note: Aphoristic phrasing states the beat's conclusion twice with minimal added information, verging on a pseudo-profound flourish rather than earned insight.
findings.Fix: Trim to one clause: 'It had been put somewhere, by someone who expected it back.'

findings.Quote: Three weeks had taught her that the system she worked inside ran on a logic she could write down without needing to understand it.
findings.Note: Reads as a stated-truth aphorism about her own competence rather than a grounded observation; slightly abstract for the concrete scene around it.
findings.Fix: Anchor it to a specific prior instance rather than a general claim.

findings.Quote: three facts that didn't belong anywhere on their own and lined up together the moment she stopped trying to file them apart
findings.Note: Slightly overwritten/abstract phrasing that tells the reader how to feel about the facts' significance rather than letting the list itself carry it.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause and let the three facts stand unglossed, or replace with a more concrete image of alignment.

findings.Quote: more times than she could count without looking
findings.Note: Hedge phrase that gestures at frequency without committing to a concrete image; slightly filler.
findings.Fix: Cut to 'more times than she liked' or give an actual number/instance.

findings.Quote: She had built her whole method on finishing what she started.
findings.Note: Borders on telling-not-showing a character trait as a summary statement rather than dramatized behavior.
findings.Fix: Let the paperwork list itself demonstrate the method; trim the explanatory sentence.

findings.Quote: stopped believing a facilities ticket did anything but generate a confirmation number of its own
findings.Note: slightly overworked phrasing for a small bureaucratic irony, tips toward telling the cynicism rather than just showing it
findings.Fix: trim to 'stopped believing a facilities ticket did anything at all'

findings.Quote: A woman who had been, for one morning, the only person in the district who understood what Yemina was looking at before Yemina fully understood it herself.
findings.Note: fragment tips into telling-not-showing, asserting significance rather than letting the two-years detail do the work
findings.Fix: integrate into the prior sentence or cut the standalone fragment

findings.Quote: a field that ended was a field a supervisor could close without asking her a question she had no answer for
findings.Fix: tighten to avoid the doubled abstraction — e.g. 'a closed field was one nobody would ask her about again.'

findings.Quote: The color of a thing that had stopped being argued with.
findings.Note: Purple abstraction that doesn't quite parse as a literal description of a color — clever-sounding but strains under scrutiny.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it: 'The color of something that had given up arguing about what it was.'

findings.Quote: Not a wall. Not a locked door. A locker with no name on it
findings.Note: The anaphoric negation-then-reveal is a slightly worn rhetorical device that risks feeling like a writerly flourish rather than earned observation.
findings.Fix: Collapse to one line: 'Just a locker with no name on it, in a freight yard she had no reason to visit.'

findings.Quote: That was the entry she couldn't write, and the only one that mattered: destination unknown, custody accepted, by whom the record does not show.
findings.Note: Aphoristic summary that tells us the significance rather than showing it; leans toward pseudo-profound cadence.
findings.Fix: Cut the editorializing clause and let the bureaucratic phrase stand alone: 'Destination unknown, custody accepted, by whom the record does not show.'
